sections.theory:
ii. Reforming Process

The process of reforming of hydrocarbon is carried out by using heat, pressure and/or catalyst in order to obtain desired products. In this process, heavy naphtha is converted into aromatics such as benzene, toluene and xylene as well as hydrogen as by-product. Reforming process breaks down the molecules of low octane rating naphtha into high octane gasoline blending components (reformates). It is one of the most important processes in oil refineries.

Fractional Distillation of Petroleum

Petroleum in the unrefined form is called crude oil. It is a naturally occurring thick viscous brown or greenish black liquid, which is obtained from earth crust. The crude oil consists of different substances. These substances in crude oil are miscible. Therefore they do not separate out into layers. Thus, fractional distillation, which is carried out in the fractionating towers, is used in refining petroleum. Fractional distillation is the process of heating up a mixture containing different substances with different boiling points and after condensation drawing the different fractions off. Each fraction is not a pure compound but is a mixture of different hydrocarbons with similar boiling points. Crude oil is first treated to remove the sulphur or sulphur compounds that may be present. The cleaned hydrocarbon material is then distilled and fractions with various boiling ranges are collected. (Figure 22.1).

Figure 22.1 Fractional distillation column.

The main goal of refinery operations is the production of gasoline. The principal fractions obtained during fractional distillation are given in Table 22.3.

sections.content:
ii. Reforming Process

The process of reforming of hydrocarbon is carried out by using heat, pressure and/or catalyst in order to obtain desired products. In this process, heavy naphtha is converted into aromatics such as benzene, toluene and xylene as well as hydrogen as by-product. Reforming process breaks down the molecules of low octane rating naphtha into high octane gasoline blending components (reformates). It is one of the most important processes in oil refineries.

Fractional Distillation of Petroleum

Petroleum in the unrefined form is called crude oil. It is a naturally occurring thick viscous brown or greenish black liquid, which is obtained from earth crust. The crude oil consists of different substances. These substances in crude oil are miscible. Therefore they do not separate out into layers. Thus, fractional distillation, which is carried out in the fractionating towers, is used in refining petroleum. Fractional distillation is the process of heating up a mixture containing different substances with different boiling points and after condensation drawing the different fractions off. Each fraction is not a pure compound but is a mixture of different hydrocarbons with similar boiling points. Crude oil is first treated to remove the sulphur or sulphur compounds that may be present. The cleaned hydrocarbon material is then distilled and fractions with various boiling ranges are collected. (Figure 22.1).

Figure 22.1 Fractional distillation column.

The main goal of refinery operations is the production of gasoline. The principal fractions obtained during fractional distillation are given in Table 22.3.
